change_interpretations.engineering_summary: VCU-BRK-03 was updated to add a strict latency requirement: emergency brake commands must be issued within 80 ms of input. Tests verifying emergency brake execution or priority must now be checked against this 80 ms limit.

assessments.reason: TV-001 measures accelerator pedal step response time under unchanged requirement VCU-DR-01. Workshop notes emphasize that positive torque latency and brake command latency are measured on different clocks and must not be conflated.
evidence: Procedure checks requested positive torque within 100 ms of pedal validation
Workshop note: 'Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks'
assessments.recommended_action: No change required; keep existing test baseline.

assessments.reason: TV-002 exercises emergency brake priority over pedal demand under VCU-BRK-03, but previous test evidence recorded no timing metrics. It cannot be determined from past evidence whether the brake command latency meets the new 80 ms limit.
evidence: Comment: 'Timing not reported in old evidence'
New VCU-BRK-03 requirement specifies 80 ms latency limit
assessments.recommended_action: Re-run TV-002 with timing logging enabled to confirm brake command latency satisfies the 80 ms threshold.

assessments.reason: Despite missing requirement links, TV-003 measures high-load accelerator demand response time (92 ms) against a 95 ms target. It does not exercise emergency brake functions.
evidence: Comment: 'Legacy suite still checks 95 ms tolerance'
Workshop note: 'Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks'
assessments.recommended_action: Restore missing link to VCU-DR-01 during requirement catalog cleanup.

assessments.reason: TV-004 directly measures emergency brake command latency. Its existing procedure target (100 ms) and previous measured result (88 ms) are invalidated by the tightened 80 ms requirement in VCU-BRK-03.
evidence: Procedure specifies target brake command latency within 100 ms
Revised VCU-BRK-03 requirement sets maximum latency to 80 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Update procedure pass criterion to 80 ms and re-run test to evaluate compliance.

assessments.reason: TV-005 checks wheel-speed sensor fault logging and degraded mode entry under unchanged requirement VCU-DGN-04.
TV-006 verifies operating mode audit logging under unchanged requirement VCU-LOG-05.
TV-007 has an unvalidated 'TBD' requirement reference, has never been run, and notes unassigned ownership.
evidence: Comment: 'Ownership and source link to be clarified'
assessments.recommended_action: Consult system engineering to assign test ownership and link to a valid requirement.

assessments.reason: TV-008 references unknown requirement VCU-OLD-88, indicating broken traceability due to a catalog revision.
assessments.recommended_action: Reconcile legacy requirement VCU-OLD-88 with system engineering to update or retire the test.

assessments.reason: TV-009 compares torque profile ramps between Sport and Comfort modes under unchanged requirement VCU-MOD-06 and includes no emergency brake timing assertion.
TV-010 evaluates pedal signal spike filtering under unchanged requirement VCU-DR-02.
evidence: Procedure checks 7 ms false pedal pulse filtering

assessments.reason: TV-011 verifies torque cancellation upon emergency brake input under VCU-BRK-03, but previous evidence contains no response latency measurements to confirm compliance with the new 80 ms requirement.
evidence: Procedure verifies positive torque drop when emergency braking is requested
Previous PASS result lacks quantitative timing data
assessments.recommended_action: Re-run TV-011 with latency measurement enabled to confirm compliance with the 80 ms response threshold.

assessments.reason: TV-012 tests ECU power-up startup timing (433 ms vs 500 ms limit), which is completely unrelated to emergency brake override logic.
evidence: Procedure measures power cycle readiness within 500 ms
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this specification change.
